title: Lee et al. 2019 (Motor Imagery) — EEG dataset and OpenBMI toolbox for three BCI paradigms: an investigation into BCI illiteracy
description: A comprehensive EEG dataset comprising 54 healthy subjects performing three major brain-computer interface (BCI) paradigms—motor imagery, event-related potentials, and steady-state visually evoked potentials—across two sessions. The dataset investigates BCI illiteracy rates and performance variations, revealing that 53.7% of users exhibited motor imagery illiteracy while all participants successfully controlled at least one BCI paradigm type.
methods_description: EEG data acquired at 1000 Hz sampling rate from 62 Ag/AgCl electrodes using BrainAmp amplifier with nose reference and AFz ground. Impedance maintained below 10 kOhm. Subjects performed binary left/right hand motor imagery tasks with visual arrow cues over 4-second trials across two sessions, each containing offline training and online test phases of 100 trials. Auxiliary EMG recordings from 4 channels captured arm muscle activity. Resting state and artifact data also recorded.
